question: How should parents be treated?
summary: The Torah and the wisdom literature hand down an unambiguous rule: honor your father and mother. It is one of the Ten Commandments, repeated in Deuteronomy, echoed in Proverbs, and reaffirmed by Paul as "the first commandment with promise." Then the Gospels put words in Jesus' mouth that run the other way — disciples must "hate" father and mother, leave a father unburied, and call no man on earth their father. One stream demands you honor your parents; the other demands you subordinate or reject them for the sake of the kingdom. They cannot both be the operative standard at the same time.

reconcile.connective: Commentators read the Gospel "hate" as a Semitic idiom of comparative preference, so loving Christ more leaves the command to honor parents intact.

discrepancy.connective: The sharpest objection is pressed by E. P. Sanders, who argues that "let the dead bury their dead" required a follower to violate the binding duty to bury and honor a parent — a rare point where Jesus contravened the Mosaic law.

excerpts.excerpt_text: And hate not - Matthew, Mat 10:37, expresses the true meaning of this word, when he says, He who loveth his father and mother More than me.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly defuses the central tension: 'hate' (Luke 14:26) is glossed as a Hebrew idiom meaning 'love less than me' (Matt 10:37), so it does not negate honoring parents.
excerpts.source_note_text: And hate not - Matthew, Mat 10:37, expresses the true meaning of this word, when he says, He who loveth his father and mother More than me. In Mat 6:24, he uses the word hate in the same sense. When we read, Rom 9:13, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated, the meaning is simply, I have loved Jacob - the Israelites, more than Esau - the Edomites; and that this is no arbitrary interpretation of the word hate, but one agreeable to the Hebrew idiom, appears from what is said on Gen 29:30, Gen 29:31, where Leah's being hated is explained by Rachel's being loved more than Leah. See also Deu 21:15-17; and Bishop Pearce on this place. See also the notes on Mat 10:37 (note).
